subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Negative Reciprocity
description: A short lesson to help you apply Negative Reciprocity.

hook.text: A worker feels underpaid and starts coming in late, doing less, and taking longer breaks.

buildup.text: Negative reciprocity: people punish those who treat them unfairly, even when punishment costs them personally.

discovery.text: Fehr and Gachter found employees reduce effort precisely in proportion to the perceived unfairness of their wage.

twist.text: The punishment is not always visible. Quiet withdrawal, sabotage, and disengagement are costlier than open complaints.

climax.text: Fair treatment isn't ethical. It's economically rational. Perceived unfairness triggers retaliation that costs everyone.

punchline.text: Unfairness is an expense. It just shows up late.

quiz.question: How do workers respond to perceived unfair wages?
options: They reduce effort in proportion to perceived unfairness
They increase effort to earn a raise
